chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever was a stipulation before the marriage, the marriage nullified it, and whatever was after the marriage, then it is valid.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the term is specified, then it is Mut'ah, and if the term is not specified, then it is a lasting marriage.'
ai.seo_question: How does one distinguish between Mut'ah and permanent marriage based on stipulations of time?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that pre-contractual stipulations are generally nullified by the marriage bond, whereas post-contractual conditions remain valid, a principle crucial for understanding the flexibility of Shia marital jurisprudence. He further clarifies the distinction between Mut'ah (temporary marriage) and permanent marriage (Nikah Battn), noting that the explicit specification of a duration defines the former, while its absence indicates the latter. This ruling highlights the structural differences in contractual validity and temporal scope between the two forms of marriage in Shia fiqh.
